The '''Moshannon Valley Correctional Center''' or '''Moshannon Valley Processing Center''' is an Immigration & Customs Enforcement building located in [[Decatur Township, Clearfield County, Pennsylvania]], just outside of  the borough of [[Philipsburg, Centre County, Pennsylvania|Philipsburg]] in the larger [[Moshannon Valley]] area. The facility is privately operated by the [[GEO Group]] under contract with the [[U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement]]. It has a capacity of 1,878<ref>{{cite web| title=Moshannon Valley Correctional Facility| url=https://www.geogroup.com/FacilityDetail/FacilityID/67| website=geogroup.com| access-date=May 19, 2020}}</ref> and is the largest ICE detention center in the [[Northeast United States]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last=Nathan |first=Debbie |date=2025-08-07 |title=Chinese ICE Detainee Dies by Suicide at Pennsylvania Detention Center |url=https://theintercept.com/2025/08/07/ice-detained-suicide-pennsylvania-geo-group/ |access-date=2025-08-08 |website=The Intercept |language=en-US}}</ref> It originally closed on March 31, 2021, after the [[Federal Bureau of Prisons]] decided to not exercise the contract renewal option.<ref name="businesswire.com">{{cite web| title=The GEO Group Announces Decision by Federal Bureau of Prisons To Not Renew Its Contract for the Moshannon Valley Correctional Facility in Pennsylvania| url=https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20210120005089/en/The-GEO-Group-Announces-Decision-by-Federal-Bureau-of-Prisons-To-Not-Renew-Its-Contract-for-the-Moshannon-Valley-Correctional-Facility-in-Pennsylvania| website=businesswire.com| access-date=May 5, 2021}}</ref> The facility opened back up in November 2021 after receiving a contract with ICE.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|last=Corcino|first=Jeff|title=Moshannon Valley Correctional Facility to reopen|url=http://www.theprogressnews.com/news/local/moshannon-valley-correctional-facility-to-reopen/article_4091d4cb-9912-5d30-a05e-48d44affffe8.html|access-date=2021-08-08|website=The Progress|language=en}}</ref>

==History==
The facility began accepting prisoners in April 2006 <ref name="post-gazette.com">{{cite news |last=Bucsko |first= Mike |date=April 30, 2006 |url=https://www.post-gazette.com/frontpage/2006/04/30/Texas-firm-to-operate-Pa-s-1st-private-prison-in-Clearfield/stories/200604300138 |title=Texas firm to operate Pa.'s 1st private prison in Clearfield|newspaper=[[Pittsburgh Post-Gazette]]}}</ref> and continued to expand up until originally closing in 2021. At opening it was the first privately owned prison in Pennsylvania.<ref name="post-gazette.com"/> It housed low-security, nonviolent criminal aliens who had less than 5 years on their remaining sentences.

In September 2013 the future of Moshannon Valley's continued operation was said to hinge on a federal contractual decision between this facility and the [[Northeast Ohio Correctional Center]], privately run by the [[Corrections Corporation of America]] near [[Youngstown, Ohio]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Carroll |first=Matt |date=September 22, 2013 |url=http://www.centredaily.com/2013/09/22/3802495/future-of-moshannon-valley-prison.html |title=Future of Moshannon Valley prison tied to fight for federal contract |newspaper=[[Centre Daily Times]] |location=State College, Pennsylvania|access-date=February 4, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140221090200/http://www.centredaily.com/2013/09/22/3802495/future-of-moshannon-valley-prison.html |archive-date=February 21, 2014 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In December 2014 Moshannon Valley's contract was renewed by the Federal government for 5 years, with 5 one year options after that for a total of 10 years.<ref>{{cite news |last=Falce |first=Lori |date=December 29, 2014|url=http://www.centredaily.com/2014/12/29/4529720/contract-renewed-for-moshannon.html|title=Contract Renewed For Moshannon |newspaper= Centre Daily Times |location=State College, Pennsylvania}}</ref>

In August 2016, Justice Department officials announced that the FBOP would be phasing out its use of all contracted facilities, on the grounds that private prisons provided less safe and less effective services with no substantial cost savings. The agency expected to allow current contracts on its thirteen remaining private facilities to expire.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Zapotosky|first1=Matt|title=Justice Department says it will end use of private prisons|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/post-nation/wp/2016/08/18/justice-department-says-it-will-end-use-of-private-prisons/|access-date=August 19, 2016|work=Washington Post|date=August 18, 2016}}</ref>

In January 2021, it was announced that the Federal Bureau of Prisons had decided to not exercise the contract renewal option for the facility, and would allow the contract to end on March 31, 2021. GEO was expected to market the building to other federal and state agencies.<ref name="businesswire.com"/> Moshannon Valley Economic Development Partnership President Bryan Bennett said the closing was the worst economical news for the area in years, saying "The upcoming closure of the GEO Moshannon Valley facility is the worst economic news that we have received in our region in over twenty years. MVEDP believes it essential that local leaders now work with GEO Group representatives to determine if there will be any reuse opportunities."<ref>{{cite news |last=Noal |first=Julie |date=March 17, 2021 |url=http://www.theprogressnews.com/progress_news/lawmakers-leaders-discuss-future-of-geo-moshannon-valley/article_6f461c14-7583-5b7f-a84e-c80701df3699.html |title=Lawmakers, leaders discuss future of GEO Moshannon Valley |newspaper=The Progress News |location=Philipsburg, Pennsylvania| access-date=May 5, 2021}}</ref>

In August 2021, it was revealed that the GEO Group had contracted the building to ICE (U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement) to become a detention facility.<ref name=":0"/> Interest in the facility from ICE came when they lost a major contract with York County Jail last year. On September 28, 2021, the Clearfield County Commissioners approved a five-year contract that began in November 2021 and will run through November 2026.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|date=2021-09-29|title=Moshannon Valley Correctional Facility to Reopen as ICE Center|url=https://gantnews.com/2021/09/29/moshannon-valley-correctional-facility-to-reopen-as-ice-center/|access-date=2021-09-29|website=GantNews.com|language=en-US}}</ref> The facility will see some upgrades such as, and new 'no-climb' perimeter fencing. Local officials predict approximately 200 jobs were restored to the area with the potential for an additional 100 if the facility reaches capacity. Once released, detainees will be taken to either Pittsburgh or Philadelphia for travel to their final destination. The detainees will spend an average of 2–4 weeks at the institution before being relocated.<ref name=":1"/>

During the [[second presidency of Donald Trump]], the facility served as a major facility for immigrants apprehended by ICE in the [[New York City|New York]] and [[Philadelphia]] regions.<ref name=":2"/> The facility has received complaints about abusive conditions, with civil rights advocates describing it as "an oppressive environment that seemed more like a prison for convicted criminals than a temporary holding center for immigrants."<ref name=":2"/>
